pages.title: Introduction
pages.content:
## Welcome to the Wildlife

Walk a little slower and look around. Thirty new animals now live in Iekcorbar, next to the cows and sheep you already know. They are shy and rare, and each one has its own home: red deer in the forests, mallards on the river, fireflies over the swamp at night, crabs on the beach, elephants and zebras on the savanna - and in the bamboo thickets and snowy woods, the tanuki, the red-crowned crane, the golden koi and troops of macaques. New since spring: roos hopping the plains, an ostrich that outruns you, crocodiles that are logs with opinions, napping koalas, molehills (and once, a mole), rhinos in the dust, penguin colonies on the ice, a blow out in the deep ocean - orca - and red-bellied piranha shoals in the warm shallows, while scarlet macaws scream over the jungle canopy.

This is not about catching or fighting. It is about **finding, watching and recording**, like a naturalist with a field journal. No mods needed.

### What you will do

* **Explore.** Different biomes, different animals. Some come out only by day, some only at night, snails like rain.
* **Watch.** Look at an animal through a spyglass for a moment and it is written in your Field Journal.
* **Collect.** Each species is an advancement in the Wildlife tab, and some animals have a rare colouring that counts as a special find.
* **Be gentle.** Deer run if you walk up to them, bears sleep at night and are calm until hurt. Learn how each animal behaves.

### How the pages are organised

**Wildlife** explains the journal and the advancements. **Species** lists every animal and where to look for it. **Breeding and Babies** explains how to raise young animals, and **Statues** how to build a stone version of any animal.

### Good to know first

* Nothing from the normal game was removed or replaced. Wildlife is only added.
* Animals are scarce on purpose. If you see nothing, keep exploring and try another time of day.
* A **name tag** keeps an animal in place, otherwise it wanders off when nobody is near.

### Start here

1. Craft a spyglass (copper ingot and amethyst shard).
2. Read [Wildlife](/wiki?page=wildlife) to see how the journal works.
3. Pick an animal from [Species](/wiki?page=wildlife-species) and go and find it.

pages.title: Wildlife
pages.content:
## Wildlife - shy animals to find and record

Iekcorbar's countryside has new animals living next to the familiar ones: deer in the forests, mallards on the rivers, fireflies over the swamps at night, crabs scuttling along the beach - and in the east, tanuki at dusk, cranes standing in the reeds, koi gliding under the surface and macaques chattering in the trees. They are **rare and shy**, and each species only lives in its own kind of place. Nothing vanilla was removed - cows, pigs and sheep are all still there.

### How it works

1. **Get a spyglass** (copper + amethyst shard, as in vanilla).
2. **Find an animal** in the right biome. Some only come out by day, fireflies only at night, and snails like the rain. Shy species are also rarer in the wild.
3. **Approach like a naturalist, not a hunter.** Deer, zebras, cranes and songbirds bolt when an upright or sprinting player gets close; a **sneaking, still** one may come near enough. Tortoises hide, hedgehogs curl - even from a friendly boot.
4. **Watch it through the spyglass** until the dots fill. A calm species takes a second; a shy one up to four - and **from far away it goes twice as fast** while standing right in front of it takes twice as long. A bolted animal resets the meter.
5. **Read your journal** with **/wildlife journal**, or craft a **Field Journal** (book + feather + wheat seeds) and right-click it. Species you haven't found yet show a hint - recorded ones show a **true fact** and a **myth** about the animal. Some of those facts surprise even old hands.

### Rare looks

Now and then an animal has a rare colouring - an albino deer, a blue morpho butterfly, a capybara wearing a yuzu. Spotting one gives its own (hidden) advancement and a mark in your journal.

### Advancements

Open the advancement screen and look for the **Wildlife** tab: one advancement per species, one per rare look, and milestones for 5 species, 10 species, every species, your first rare find and 5 rare finds. There is also a separate **Zoo** tab with advancements for building your own zoo: placing props, building entrances, enclosures, comfort areas, paths and decorations.

### Commands

* **/wildlife** - open the Wildlife menu: every species (found ones show details and a click points you to the nearest one), your totals, and shortcuts to the journal, your dragons and the zoo help.
* **/wildlife journal** - read your Field Journal.
* **/wildlife stats [player]** - see how many species you have recorded.
* **/wildlife list [filter]** - list all species and where they live.
* **/wildlife find <species>** - find the nearest animal of that species.
* **/wildlife tamed** - list your tamed dragons.
* **/wildlife spawn <species> [rare] [baby]** - spawn an animal (staff only).
* **/wildlife egg <species> [player]** - give a spawn egg (staff only).
* **/wildlife give <player> <item>** - give an item (staff only).
* **/wildlife info** - server info (staff only).
* **/wildlife reload** - reload config (staff only).
* **/wildlife remove <radius>** - remove animals in a radius (staff only).

### Zoo-builder

Build your own zoo with craftable decor props: doors, toilets, cobblestone paths, welcome/exit signs, flower boxes, picnic tables, parasols, first aid posts and brick walls. Place ticket kiosks, turnstiles and gates to create a working zoo with tickets. Animals can be kept on leads or with name tags. Statues of every animal can be crafted from stone and the animal's drop item.

### Materials from the animals

Adult animals that did not starve can leave a raw material behind: **ivory** (elephant), **antler** (deer), **bear pelt**, **crocodile hide**, **striped hide** (zebra), **kangaroo hide**, **ostrich**, **crane** and **macaw** plumes, **penguin down**, **rhino horn**, **koi scale**, **orca** and **piranha teeth**, and **brass scrap** from a steam dragon. A rare look drops double. Brewers use the koi scale in the Sakagura *Golden Koi Sake*; the Kitchen and Sakagura recognise all of them as ingredients.

### Feeding in the zoo

Only animals that belong to someone (a name tag or a lead) get hungry; wild animals find their own food. Put food in a **feeding trough** (one kind at a time, up to 32): every few seconds it feeds the hungriest animal within six blocks that actually eats that food, and never one that is already well fed. Hunger is remembered across restarts. A starving kept animal slows down and drops nothing.

### Graveyard spawning

Wraiths now spawn at night near graveyards (soul sand/soul soil clusters). They are sfeer-wezen: they drift, shed mist, moan softly and vanish at dawn. They are not in the Field Journal and cannot be bred.

### Behaviour worth knowing

* **Deer and lizards** run when you come close - sneak to get near.
* **Hedgehogs and snails** curl up or hide in their shell; **tortoises** pull in their head and legs.
* **Brown bears** are calm until you hurt them, sleep at night, eat sweet berries - and by day you may see one sit at the riverbank, fish a **salmon** out of the water and eat it on the spot.
* **Wild boars** charge when they feel cornered.
* **Butterflies** pollinate: they flutter over your wheat, carrots, potatoes and beetroots and ripen them a step faster, and flower patches near them spread themselves to bare grass. A field with butterflies visibly outgrows one without.
* **Hunter's trophy**: an animal you have **recorded in your Field Journal first** sometimes leaves its own **statue** as a trophy when you take it down (rarer animals, bigger chance). The naturalist's deal: observe, then hunt.
* **Capybaras** sometimes give a duck or a songbird a ride.
* **Lizards** can drop their tail when hit (it grows back). **Crabs** sometimes drop a claw: hold a **Crab Claw** in your off hand to reach one block further.
* A **name tag** keeps an animal around; unnamed wildlife wanders off when nobody is near. So does a **lead**: an animal you put on a lead stays.
* Only adult bears and boars ever fight back. Every other animal is harmless, and so are their young.
* **Young animals** exist too, and you can raise them: see [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding).

See [Wildlife Species](/wiki?page=wildlife-species) for where each animal lives.

pages.title: Wildlife Species
pages.content:
* [Species](/wiki?page=wildlife-species-species)
* [Spirits and placed creatures](/wiki?page=wildlife-species-spirits-and-placed)

pages.title: Species
pages.content:
| Animal | Where to look | When |
|---|---|---|
| Red Deer | forests, taiga, meadows, cherry groves | day and night |
| Brown Bear | old taiga, dark forests | day and night (sleeps at night) |
| Wild Boar | forests, dark forests, wooded badlands | day and night |
| Mallard | rivers, swamps, mangroves | day and night |
| Monarch Butterfly | flower forests, meadows, plains, cherry groves | by day |
| Firefly | swamps, mangroves, forests | at night |
| Garden Snail | damp forests, swamps (more in the rain) | day and night |
| Hedgehog | forests, plains, meadows | day and night |
| Capybara | jungle, swamp and mangrove riverbanks | day and night |
| Tortoise | savannas, jungles, badlands | by day |
| Wall Lizard | deserts, badlands, savannas, stony shores | by day |
| Shore Crab | beaches, mangroves, stony shores | day and night |
| Songbird (jay, cardinal, canary, sparrow) | forests, plains, meadows | by day |
| Emperor Dragonfly | above rivers and swamps | by day |
| African Elephant | savannas, in small herds | day and night |
| Plains Zebra | savannas, in groups | day and night |
| Red Kangaroo | plains, savanna edges | day and night |
| Common Ostrich | savannas, deserts | by day |
| Siamese Crocodile | swamps, jungles, mangroves | day and night |
| Koala | jungle and bamboo, asleep | day and night |
| European Mole | lawns and forest edges (follow the molehills) | day and night |
| White Rhinoceros | savannas, at wallows | day and night |
| Emperor Penguin | ice coasts and frozen shores | by day, in colonies |
| Orca | the deep ocean | day and night, very rare |
| Red-bellied Piranha | warm rivers and swamps | day and night, in shoals |
| Scarlet Macaw | over the jungle | by day |
| Tanuki | bamboo thickets, old forests | at night |
| Red-Crowned Crane | swamps, marshes, river flats | day and night (always in pairs) |
| Koi | rivers, swamp pools | day and night (in the water!) |
| Japanese Macaque | bamboo, snowy forests | by day, in troops |

The **African Elephant** is the biggest animal around and the **Plains Zebra** always walks in a group. Both have a rare look too: a white elephant and a golden zebra. From the east come four more: the night-wandering **Tanuki** (rarely seen, charcoal-black on lucky nights), the stately **Red-Crowned Crane** that stays with its partner for life, the **Koi** gliding just under the surface (the all-gold one is the famous Golden Koi), and noisy troops of **Japanese Macaques** in the bamboo and snowy woods.

And everywhere their own little rumours: a fresh **molehill** in the lawn means a **Mole** has been working below - see one of them and you are lucky. **Penguins** bray like donkeys on the ice, **koalas** sleep the day away, and a **crocodile** is exactly as still as it looks. Out in the deep ocean, an **Orca** surfaces so rarely that nobody plans on it; near the jungle water, a shimmering shoal of **Piranhas** is a reminder not to swim there hungry, and the **Scarlet Macaw** overhead will happily repeat back whatever you said about it.

Animals are scarce on purpose: if you don't see one, keep exploring - and try a different time of day.

Back to [Wildlife Species](/wiki?page=wildlife-species)

pages.title: Spirits and placed creatures
pages.content:
Not everything with a model is an animal. The **Wraith** is a floating, hooded shadow in a torn robe -
a creature of atmosphere for dark, quiet corners: a crypt, an old tower, a swamp at midnight. It never
hunts and never flees; it drifts slowly up and down, sheds a little mist off its hem and a cold spark
at its hood, moans softly when someone stands near, and it **vanishes when the morning comes** - it
belongs to the dark only.

Wraiths are deliberately outside everything that makes an animal an animal: they are **not in the Field
Journal** (no page, no advancement, no spyglass record), they **cannot be bred** and have no babies,
there is **no spawn egg and no statue** for them, and **no recipe** anywhere makes one. They are placed
by staff with `/wildlife spawn wraith` (an admin command; they are also switched off in the wild-spawner
config). So if you meet one, it was put there on purpose - enjoy the chill.

Back to [Wildlife Species](/wiki?page=wildlife-species)

pages.title: Breeding and Babies
pages.content:
## Breeding and babies

Every animal can have young - even the bees and the songbirds. Raising them is slow on purpose.


* [How to breed](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-how-to-breed)
* [What to feed](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-what-to-feed)
* [Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-babies)
* [Keep a baby small](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-keep-a-baby-small)
* [Keeping your animals](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-keeping-your-animals)
* [Good to know](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-good-to-know)

pages.title: How to breed
pages.content:
1. **Right-click an adult with its food** (table below). Hearts appear: it is in love for 30 seconds.
2. Do the same to **a second animal of the same kind** within a few blocks.
3. The two walk to each other and **a baby appears**. Both parents need about 5 minutes before they can have another one.

If a lot of the same animal is already close by, the game says it is **too crowded** and nothing happens. That keeps farms small.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: What to feed
pages.content:
| Animal | Food |
|---|---|
| Red Deer | wheat, apples or carrots |
| Brown Bear | sweet berries, salmon or honey |
| Wild Boar | carrots, potatoes or beetroot |
| Mallard, Songbird | seeds |
| Monarch Butterfly | small flowers |
| Firefly | glow berries |
| Garden Snail | dried kelp or seagrass |
| Hedgehog | mushrooms |
| Capybara | melon slices or sugar cane |
| Tortoise | seagrass |
| Wall Lizard | spider eyes |
| Shore Crab | cod or kelp |
| Emperor Dragonfly | sugar |
| African Elephant | wheat, sugar cane or apples |
| Plains Zebra | wheat or hay bales |
| Tanuki | sweet berries or apples |
| Red-Crowned Crane | seeds or a fish |
| Koi | kelp or a piece of bread |
| Japanese Macaque | apples, carrots or potatoes |
| Red Kangaroo | wheat, hay or carrots |
| Common Ostrich | seeds |
| Siamese Crocodile | fish or a piece of beef |
| Koala | leaves or apples |
| European Mole | spider eyes (it really eats grubs) |
| White Rhinoceros | wheat, hay or melon |
| Emperor Penguin | fish |
| Orca | a big fish |
| Red-bellied Piranha | any raw meat |
| Scarlet Macaw | seeds or cocoa beans |

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Babies
pages.content:
A baby is **half the size**, with a big head, and it is harmless - even a bear cub or a boar piglet. It grows up after about 20 minutes. Feeding a baby its food makes it grow a little faster.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Keep a baby small
pages.content:
Give a baby a **golden dandelion** and it **stays a baby**. Give it another golden dandelion and it starts growing again. A baby kept small is yours: it stays where you left it, even when nobody is around.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Keeping your animals
pages.content:
Wild animals wander off when nobody is near. A **name tag**, a **lead**, or a golden dandelion (for babies) keeps an animal for good. Perfect for a zoo.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Good to know
pages.content:
* A baby born next to its parents looks like them. Rare parents have a good chance of a rare baby.
* A grown-up that was on a lead slips out of it and the lead drops to the ground.
* Young animals now and then show up on their own in a bigger group.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Statues
pages.content:
## Animal statues

Every animal can be placed as a **true-size statue**, in three versions: the animal, its **rare look** and a **baby**. They are decoration for your zoo or garden.


* [Crafting](/wiki?page=wildlife-statues-crafting)
* [Placing and moving](/wiki?page=wildlife-statues-placing-and-moving)

pages.title: Crafting
pages.content:
Craft them on a crafting table, no pattern needed. Use stone and the **item that animal drops** (the same one shown on its advancement):

| Statue | Ingredients |
|---|---|
| Adult | 3 stone + the animal's item |
| Baby | 2 stone + the animal's item |
| Rare | 3 stone + the animal's item + 1 amethyst shard |

For example a deer statue is 3 stone and leather.

Back to [Statues](/wiki?page=wildlife-statues)

pages.title: Placing and moving
pages.content:
* Right-click a block with the statue to place it. It turns to face you.
* **Hit it a few times** to pick it up again.
* The elephant statue is three blocks tall, so leave some room.

Statues stand still; the real animals are found in the wild. They go well with the **Zoo** props: fences, gates, troughs and info boards.

Back to [Statues](/wiki?page=wildlife-statues)

pages.title: Steam Dragons
pages.content:
## Steam Dragons

A Steam Dragon is brass over an iron frame with a furnace ticking behind its ribs. It lives deep in the big caverns, and it can become your companion, your mount and your pack animal.


* [Finding and taming](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons-finding-and-taming)
* [Commands for your dragon](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons-commands-for-your-dragon)
* [Riding](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons-riding)
* [The Dragon Whistle](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons-the-dragon-whistle)
* [Saddlebags](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons-saddlebags)
* [Hunger](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons-hunger)
* [Dyes - a new coat of paint](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons-dyes-a-new-coat-of-paint)
* [Eggs](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons-eggs)
* [Good to know](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons-good-to-know)

pages.title: Finding and taming
pages.content:
* You do not see it so much as hear it: follow the hiss through the large caves, far underground.
* Feed it **coal or charcoal** (right-click). Each lump has a 35 % chance; the furnace decides when it trusts you.
* A tamed dragon follows you, circles at a distance, and lands a few blocks away when you stand still.

Back to [Steam Dragons](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons)

pages.title: Commands for your dragon
pages.content:
Look at your dragon (or stand close) and use:

* **/wildlife pet** - a small menu: sit or stand, come here, rename, saddlebags and set free.
* **/wildlife pet list** - your dragons and where they are.
* **/wildlife pet sit | stand | come** - the same as the menu buttons.
* **/wildlife pet name <name>** - give it a name (24 characters).
* **/wildlife pet bag** - open the saddlebags.
* **/wildlife pet release confirm** - set it free for good.

Sneak + right-click with an empty hand also makes it sit or stand.

Back to [Steam Dragons](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons)

pages.title: Riding
pages.content:
Right-click with an empty hand to climb on. W/A/S/D steers where you look, space climbs, back descends, sprint is faster. With no input it hovers. You take no fall or wall damage on the saddle, and stepping off in mid-air gives you a soft landing (Slow Falling for a few seconds).

Back to [Steam Dragons](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons)

pages.title: The Dragon Whistle
pages.content:
Craft it from a **copper ingot, an iron nugget and a coal**. Right-click: every tamed dragon of yours in the same world flies to you, even one that was far away in an unloaded part of the world. Four seconds between whistles. A dragon in another world (such as the Nether) cannot come.

Back to [Steam Dragons](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons)

pages.title: Saddlebags
pages.content:
Right-click your dragon with a **chest** to fit saddlebags (nine slots). Open them with **/wildlife pet bag** or from the menu while the dragon is within eight blocks. The contents stay with the dragon through restarts. If the dragon dies, everything drops where it fell.

Back to [Steam Dragons](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons)

pages.title: Hunger
pages.content:
A dragon you keep gets hungry over time. Below half it flies slower, and when it is starving it is very slow. Feed it **coal** (right-click) to restore hunger. A well fed dragon (90 and up) flies a little faster. The menu shows its hunger.

Back to [Steam Dragons](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons)

pages.title: Dyes - a new coat of paint
pages.content:
Right-click your dragon with a dye to change its look:

| Dye | Look |
|---|---|
| Orange | Brass (the original) |
| Red | Sakagura |
| Yellow | Kitchen |
| Blue | Kura |
| Green | Verdigris |

Its name, saddlebags, hunger and owner stay. Rare looks (the gilded dragon) are not affected by dyes, and a dyed dragon loses its rare look.

Back to [Steam Dragons](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons)

pages.title: Eggs
pages.content:
Two tamed dragons that are fed coal at the same time lay a **Dragon Egg** instead of a baby. Carry it in your inventory: after about eight minutes (server setting) it hatches into a baby dragon that belongs to you. Only the owner of the parents can hatch the egg.

You can also make a **nest**: sneak and right-click a **hay block** with the egg. It rests on top of the straw and stays warm without you; it hatches when its keeper is around. Sneak + right-click the straw with an empty hand takes the egg back, and breaking the hay block frees it.

Back to [Steam Dragons](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons)

pages.title: Good to know
pages.content:
* A grown-up baby keeps its owner and saddlebags.
* A dragon is made of brass: it cannot suffocate, drown or take fall damage. Fire and lava still hurt.
* If you teleport far away (home, warp, tpa), your dragon follows if it was within about 40 blocks and is not sitting.

Back to [Steam Dragons](/wiki?page=wildlife-dragons)
